data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's criterion classifies the system as efficient whenever translation overhead T_O exceeds owner solution latency S_L. But its own countercondition concedes that rejecting a vastly more robust translated solution on this basis 'may still constitute suppression of quality in favor of speed.' Thus the proposed T_O vs S_L test does not actually distinguish suppression from efficiency as the problem requires; it can label a suppressive rejection as efficient whenever translation is costly, which is precisely the regime where suppression is most likely.
